title: The Three Travelers and the Loaf of Bread (MR)
summary: Three travelers have only one loaf of bread left. Two scheme to claim the bread through a dream contest, but the third traveler outsmarts them both.
full_text:
Three travelers—a scholar, an astrologer, and a simple farmer—were journeying together across a barren desert tract toward Agra. As night fell, they discovered that their provisions were completely exhausted, save for a single small loaf of sweet wheat bread.

The loaf was barely enough to feed one hungry man.

The scholar and the astrologer, feeling superior to the simple farmer, schemed to take the bread for themselves.

The scholar proposed: 'Brothers, let us sleep tonight. In the morning, each of us shall recount the dream he experienced. He who has had the most wondrous, celestial dream shall eat the loaf of bread alone!'

The farmer agreed, and all three lay down to sleep beneath the stars.

At sunrise, the three men gathered around the bread.

The scholar boasted: 'In my dream last night, angels descended from heaven in a golden chariot, lifted my soul to the gardens of paradise, where I conversed with the ancient philosophers and drank ambrosia from crystalline fountains! Surely, no dream can surpass mine!'

The astrologer claimed: 'My dream was even greater! In my dream, my spirit flew across the cosmos, past the rings of Saturn and the blazing stars, unlocking the secrets of destiny and the foundations of time itself! My dream was far more wondrous!'

The two clever men smiled, confident that the poor, illiterate farmer could never match their visions.

The scholar turned to the farmer: 'And what did you dream, peasant?'

The farmer scratched his head and said with a sheepish grin:

'Well, brothers... in my dream last night, I saw the scholar being carried away to heaven in a golden chariot, and I saw the astrologer flying past the stars into outer space!

'I thought to myself: "My two companions have gone to paradise and the stars, and they will never return to this dusty earth! And even if they do return, they have surely feasted on celestial ambrosia and starlight!"

'So, fearing that the sweet loaf of bread would go stale in their absence, I woke up at midnight and ate the entire loaf of bread myself!'

The scholar and the astrologer stared in horrified disbelief, looked down at their empty basket, and gasped: 'You ate the bread?'

'Yes, every crumb!' the farmer smiled, patting his full stomach.

The dispute was recounted to Birbal at the city gates. Birbal laughed heartily:

'The farmer's dream was the only one that accomplished anything! While intellectual schemers waste their nights spinning grand illusions in the clouds, practical common sense eats the bread on earth!'

Akbar rewarded the farmer for his delightful pragmatism.
